sentences.text: Dishonestly receiving stolen property.

Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

Property, the possession whereof has been transferred by theft, or by extortion, or by robbery, and property which has been criminally misappropriated or in respect of which criminal breach of trust has been committed, is designated as "stolen property", whether the transfer has been made, or the misappropriation or breach of trust has been committed, within or without India.
But, if such property subsequently comes into the possession of a person legally entitled to the possession thereof, it then ceases to be stolen property.

The star witness of the present case is the complainant i.e. PW-1 Sh. Kailash Jain.

As per the testimony of PW-1, it has been stated by him that, at the time of the alleged incident, he alongwith his family members was residing at house no. S-29,
Parampuri, Bal Udyan Road, Uttam Nagar, Delhi.

On the date of the incident,
between 11:00 AM to 12:00 Noon, while he was standing at the gate of his house on the ground floor, 6-7 persons including one woman came there and asked him about his father Sh. Ramesh Chand Jain.
He informed them that his father was not at home.
At this, they disclosed that they are CBI officials and have warrants against his father regarding his arrest and search of the house.
They also showed their ID Cards to him alongwith the search warrants.
Upon seeing the warrants, he saw that it contained names of several persons known to him.
They also told him that there are complaints lodged by various persons against his father, regarding accumulation of money.
Then they all pushed him aside and went up-stairs for the purpose of search.

His mother and sister who were also present at the house were confined and made to sit in a separate room and he was also restrained at one place and then all of them started searching the beds, almirah, drawers etc.
During the search, they demanded keys of almirah from him, to which he told that his father was having the keys.
At this, they threatened him by showing the revolver in order to procure the keys of the almirah.
After taking the keys from him, they collected the cash and jewelry that was kept in the almirah in their bags and then they all left his house.
It is stated by PW-1 that he followed them on his scooter but was not able to catch State Vs. Kewal Kishan & Ors.
